To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the choice of the precipitant and the concentration of the solution are crucial for achieving the desired microstructural characteristics, which are essential to fabricate fully dense YAG transparent materials.

the use of ammonium hydrogen carbonate as precipitant solution is the most suitable choice to prepare YAG co-precipitated powders for transparent materials, provided that the concentration of AHC solution is 0.5 mol L−1.

(a) the use of ammonium hydrogen carbonate as precipitating agent allows the preparation of soft agglomerated powers, which are sinterable without the need of any additives, (b) the concentration of ammonium hydrogencarbonate plays a key role on the final powder characteristics and (c) the use of chlorides as precursors allows the preparation of pure materials, free from secondary phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the synthesis parameters on the processing and microstructure of YAG powders and materials.
the effect of different synthesis parameters (i.e., precipitant solution and precursors) on the powder characteristics, and the subsequent influence on the sintering behaviour and final properties.
the development of a co-precipitate route for the synthesis of high quality YAG powders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AHC, at 0.5M, is the best choice to prepare YAG co-precipitated powders, which are suitable for transparent applications.

the use of AA as precipitant is not recommended for preparing transparent YAG, because it gives rise to powders with a high degree of agglomeration, which are characterized by the formation of secondary phases during sintering.
the use of AHC as precipitant, at 0.5–0.6 M, allows the preparation of YAG powders suitable for the fabrication of transparent materials.

co-precipitated YAG powders can be successfully used to fabricate transparent materials.
